summary: Wooden tower on Jerimoth Hill, first operated 1917 and removed 1926 per FFLOS. Summit now state-owned and open; no source describes tower remains.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1926 per the register; no source describes remains at the site

access.note: Owned by the state (RIDEM) since October 2014 per Foster Preservation Society; no fee or permit. Hours differ by source: dawn to dusk (Foster Preservation Society) or 24 hours (highpoint.guide).

visit.trail_note: Small sandy parking area on Route 101 at the hill crest; short trail to the summit rock built in 2005. Entrance sign at pole 212 on the south side of the road.

events.note: Mosley family bought Richardson's property and allowed daily access; later gave the land to the state
Brown University took ownership of the highpoint and access road
Summit and access road owned by RIDEM from October 2014; Wikipedia says Brown sold the summit to the state in 2014

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 812 ft (247 m) and the Foster Preservation Society gives 812 feet; the Town of Foster gives 811 feet. The record keeps 247.5 m, which matches the register.

The 2008 register says private land with weekend hikes. Wikipedia, the Foster Preservation Society and highpoint.guide say the summit has been state-owned and open since 2014. The register predates those changes, so the story uses the later sources for access.
The Foster Preservation Society says generally dawn to dusk; highpoint.guide says 24 hours. The story reports both and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: The 1917 and 1926 dates rest on one source, the FFLOS register; no second source found. No staffing, fire or design detail beyond 'wooden tower'. The Weebly Jerimoth page has only a heading and no body text, so it is not cited. The 1917 Forest Lookouts passage is general state context and does not name Jerimoth Hill; it is cited only for that context. Register coordinates (41.85, -71.77533) sit about 280 m from the USGS highpoint coordinates the Foster Preservation Society gives (distance computed by me from the two coordinate pairs), so the tower's exact location is unclear and the story does not place it on the summit rock. Ownership and access history agree across Wikipedia, the Foster Preservation Society and highpoint.guide; hours do not. No photos added.
